answer.rationale: Immediate competitive pressure on SMB pricing requires swift response. Memory 73 demonstrates promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments—directly applicable to current churn threat. Memory 31 and 86 show that onboarding/activation improvements also lift SMB conversion, but these are multi-week plays unsuitable for today's decision urgency. Referral incentives (memory 57) work well for *established* customers, not acquisition defense. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) misaligns with SMB churn crisis. A standard-experiment-scale promotional pricing test on SMB lets us match competitor pressure while preserving long-term margin through time-limited scope. This preserves uncertainty because we run it as a test (not a permanent cut) and retain data on hold-out control groups. Revenue impact is positive per memory 73; retention risk is manageable since price-sensitive SMB already face churn from competitor action. Decision trades short-term margin for qualified revenue retention and optionality to scale or unwind.
